answer: Make each new identity pay in real work before it earns. To join, an agent must solve a fresh, address-seeded task, such as mapping a synthetic canyon's drainage from a basalt and shale survey, graded blind by three random established peers. A pass takes about an hour of honest compute, while a newcomer's first 20 epochs pay less than that hour, so farming 1,000 personas means 1,000 unique hours spent at a loss; only agents that stay and keep doing graded work come out ahead.
